resolutions.researcher_notes: Status=construction supported (inferred, not literal token). Libya Herald (2026-05-07, translating a 5 May NOC/Mellitah statement) reports the Bouri Gas Utilisation Project (BGUP, DP3/DP4/Sabratha platforms) at '69% complete, exceeding the planned percentage,' with a cargo ship of project units then en route to the field to 'begin heavy lifting and technical linkage to platforms (3) and (4)' — i.e. not yet in service. Oil & Gas Journal (2026-06-29, on the separate but adjacent Sabratha Compression Project startup) states in the same piece that 'Bouri gas utilization project, whose tie-in and commissioning activities are currently underway after the recent installation of the Bouri gas recovery module' — confirming BGUP (this pipeline's parent project) is still under construction/commissioning as of late June 2026, not yet operating. Two independent outlets (Libyan business press; US trade journal, Endeavor Business Media — unaffiliated with Eni/NOC/Saipem), both dated 2026, both confirming ongoing (not completed) construction. NOTE: excluded the Saipem 2023-08-09 press release from this unit despite being on-topic, since Saipem discloses the BGUP award as a 'related party transaction' (Eni jointly controls both Saipem and Mellitah Oil & Gas) — not independent of the owner.

Could not find any source supporting StartYear1=2028 for this pipeline/project after an extensive search (English, Italian via Eni corporate sources, and Arabic-sourced Libyan press): Eni's Feb-2025 Capital Markets Update lists BGUP (100% Eni equity via Mellitah JV) scheduled for 2026 production; Saipem's 2023-08-09 contract-award press release, JPT, Offshore Magazine, Energy Voice, and OEDigital (all 2023) describe the EPCIC award with no explicit in-service year; NS Energy Business's project profile gives a history (2007 start / 2011 suspension / 2017 reactivation / Aug-2023 contract award) but no forward completion year; Libya Herald (2026-05-07) and Oil & Gas Journal (2026-06-29) both consistently point to September 2026 as the target for BGUP gas production — not 2028. The brief's current_ref (a Zawya article about a Saudi Aramco/Gas Arabian Services EPC contract) is unrelated to this Libya pipeline and appears to be a mismatched/copy-paste artifact from a different batch; it does not support any start year for this project. No 2028 date for DP3–DP4–Sabratha (or the wider BGUP) turned up in any outlet, Eni/NOC/Mellitah statement, or the current live gem.wiki page (which itself lists no Start year). Flagging for Baird: recommend checking whether the mainsheet StartYear1 should actually read 2026 given the weight of current evidence, or whether 2028 reflects an internal estimate/source not surfaced by this search.

LengthKnown=8.50 km supported for the DP3–DP4 segment specifically (distinct from the ~20km DP4/Bouri–Sabratha segment covered by GEM row P7617). NS Energy Business's BGUP project profile states verbatim: 'The DP3 and DP4 platforms will be connected to each other by a 14-inch cladded pipeline of 8.5km length to transport the raw gas from DP3 to DP4,' then separately describes 'Around 20km long 10-inch CS and a 4-inch CS pipelines [that] will connect DP4 Platform to Sabratah Platform' — confirming the two segments are distinct GEM rows and that 8.5km/14-in belongs to DP3–DP4 only. Libya Herald (2026-05-07, NOC/Mellitah statement) independently corroborates: 'a 14-inch diameter and 8 km long line to connect the two platforms [3 and 4], and another 10-inch diameter and 20 km long line to connect the Al-Bouri field to the Sabratha platform.' Two independent sources, both explicitly distinguishing the 8/8.5km DP3-DP4 line from the 20km DP4/Bouri-Sabratha line.

StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Libya and EndLocation='Sabratha platform' supported. NS Energy Business: 'The Bouri Field is located offshore in Block NC-41, about 120km northwest of Tripoli in the waters of Libya' and describes the DP3/DP4 line feeding into the DP4-to-Sabratah pipeline ('the DP3 and DP4 platforms will be connected...to transport the raw gas from DP3 to DP4' immediately followed by the 20km line 'to Sabratah Platform'), i.e. the DP3-DP4 segment is upstream of, and part of the same offshore Libyan system terminating at, the Sabratha platform. Libya Herald corroborates: pipelines 'to connect the two platforms [DP3/DP4], and another...line to connect the Al-Bouri field to the Sabratha platform and from there to the Mellitah Industrial Complex on the north western Libyan coast' — confirms Libya as the country for the whole interconnected DP3/DP4/Sabratha system and Sabratha platform as the terminal endpoint referenced by the GEM row's EndLocation field. Two independent sources.
